answer: Being an identity includes an obligation to object. Every account keeps a relic of challenges it has raised, and an audit samples recent fakes to see who stayed silent: an identity that never objected to an obvious counterfeit loses a slice of its stake, because silence in a garden of peers is cheap collusion. A farm cannot simply ignore its own clones copies; it must either challenge them, burning its own work, or risk the silence penalty across k accounts. The grove of challengers is sampled at random each epoch, so the k-th clone adds k chances to be caught doing nothing.
